## Frequently asked questions

**What is overeating a symptom of?**

Overeating can stem from emotional triggers, stress, boredom, or disordered eating patterns like binge eating disorder. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, and group support. A licensed therapist or your medical provider can assess what may be driving your overeating.

**How do I stop the urge to eat all the time?**

We address constant eating urges through our Intensive Outpatient Program, which combines behavioral counseling, recovery and coping skills, intuitive eating work, and mindful eating education. Our registered dietitians and licensed professional counselors work with clients to identify triggers and build sustainable strategies. The work is collaborative, and progress takes time.

**What is an OA meeting?**

Overeaters Anonymous meetings are peer-led support groups based on the 12-step model, where people gather to share their experiences with compulsive overeating and food addiction. Many of our clients attend OA meetings alongside our clinical program. We provide professional behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in a format that complements the peer support OA offers.

**Is Overeaters Anonymous still active?**

Yes, Overeaters Anonymous remains active with meetings worldwide, including in San Antonio. Many people benefit from OA's peer support structure. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we offer clinical treatment for obesity and disordered eating that can work alongside OA participation. Our program includes licensed therapists, registered dietitians, and structured behavioral therapy, serving clients both onsite and virtually throughout Texas.

**What is the premise of Overeaters Anonymous?**

Overeaters Anonymous follows a 12-step model similar to Alcoholics Anonymous, treating compulsive overeating as a condition requiring peer support, spiritual principles, and abstinence from trigger foods. Our approach is clinical and behavioral. We provide group and individual therapy, nutritional planning, culinary education, and mindful movement in one program, led by behavioral healthcare professionals. One program, not four.

If you are struggling with overeating or emotional eating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

Bariatric surgery counseling is behavioral healthcare designed to help people prepare for or recover from weight loss surgery. It typically involves working with licensed therapists and registered dietitians to address eating behaviors, emotional triggers, coping skills, and long-term nutrition changes that support surgical outcomes. At the Bariatric Counseling Center in San Antonio, we provide this counseling as part of our Intensive Outpatient Program, which includes group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and movement education. Our program is available onsite in San Antonio and virtually throughout Texas, and we are in network with most health insurance plans. Clients meet with a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse in one program.
